appliesTo: Alabama public K-12 schools and the State Department of Education

sources.curriculum: § 16-46B-2(a)(1) — 'each public high school shall offer at least one authentic computer science course from a department-approved list'
sources.graduationReq: § 16-46B-7(c)(1) — 'Beginning with the graduating class of 2032, all public school students shall demonstrate digital literacy by earning at least one credit in a department-approved, high school or college-level computer science course'

exposure.enforcer: § 16-46B-2(e) — 'The enforcement of this section shall comply with Section 16-1-11.1.'

flags: AI content is definitional only: § 16-46B-1(2) expands 'computer science' to include 'their emerging technologies, including, but not limited to, artificial intelligence' — no AI-specific duties are imposed
Graduation requirement phases in with the class of 2032 (§ 16-46B-7(c)(1)); course-content mandate begins with students graduating in the 2031-2032 school year (§ 16-46B-2(d))
Enforcement routed by cross-reference to Section 16-1-11.1; no penalty stated in this text
